title: Intrinsic single crystals of MnTe altermagnet
authors: Kim-Khuong Huynh, Michael Anthony Quintero, Martin Klanjšek, Tilen Knaflič, Yuta Ishii, Norimasa Sasabe, Nhu-Quynh T. Phan, Frej Søren Rattenborg, Yuichi Yamasaki, Denis Arčon, Bo Brummerstedt Iversen
abstract: We report the synthesis methodology, structure, and intrinsic properties of ultra-high quality single crystals of MnTe, an archetypal altermagnet. The crystals, obtained from self-flux method, are nearly free from crystal imperfections and disproportionate chemical compositions as seen by various investigation methods. In measurements under quasi free-standing configuration minimizing stress induced effects, the crystals exhibit complex and anisotropic domain kinetics in both superheating and supercooling regimes around the altermagnetic transition at $T_{\mathrm{N}} = 310\,\mathrm{K}$. An Anderson insulating state is observed below $T_{\mathrm{MI}}\approx 150\,\mathrm{K}$ with a carrier density of about $1.6\times 10^{17}\,\mathrm{cm}^{-3}$, being sharply contrast to metallic states usually seen in Te-deficit samples. Nevertheless, hallmarks of altermagnetism, anomalous Hall effect and X-ray magnetic circular dichroism signal, are robust in this intrinsic limit, however with significantly reduced magnitudes.
summary: This work reports on high-quality single crystals of MnTe to investigate its intrinsic altermagnetic properties. By using advanced measurements like EPR, NMR, and transport studies, the authors characterize complex domain kinetics near the magnetic transition and observe a low-temperature Anderson insulating state. The findings establish these materials as crucial platforms for studying strongly correlated phenomena in clean crystalline environments.
main_problem: To study the intrinsic magnetic, electronic, and domain kinetics properties of MnTe, an archetypal altermagnet, by synthesizing ultra-high quality single crystals free from chemical imperfections.
main_result: The synthesized crystals exhibit robust hallmarks of altermagnetism (AHE, XMCD) alongside complex anisotropic domain kinetics near the Néel temperature ($T_N$), and transition into an Anderson insulating state at lower temperatures.
method: The study employs a combination of advanced characterization techniques including transport measurements ($ho(T)$, Seebeck coefficient), magnetic susceptibility, Electron Paramagnetic Resonance (EPR), and Nuclear Magnetic Resonance (NMR) on single crystals grown via self-flux methods.
model_or_system: The physical system is intrinsic single crystals of MnTe, which exhibits altermagnetism. The research probes the interplay between magnetic ordering, charge localization (Anderson insulating state), and structural/mechanical stress effects in this strongly correlated material.
key_observables: Anomalous Hall effect (AHE) signals, anisotropic hysteresis loops in magnetic susceptibility ($\chi$), resistivity ($ho_{xx}$), Seebeck coefficient ($S_{xx}$), EPR linewidth divergence near $T_N$, and Variable Range Hopping (VRH) behavior below $T_{	ext{MI}}$.
important_parameters: Altermagnetic transition temperature ($T_N \approx 310\,\mathrm{K}$), Metal-Insulator Transition temperature ($T_{	ext{MI}} \approx 150\,\mathrm{K}$), and carrier density ($\sim 1.6	imes 10^{17}\,\mathrm{cm}^{-3}$).
main_assumptions: The primary assumption is that the synthesized crystals represent the intrinsic limit, minimizing extrinsic effects like Te-deficiency or mechanical stress.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate crystal structure confirmation (SCXRD), anisotropic magnetic hysteresis loops around $T_N$, temperature dependence of transport properties ($ho_{xx}, S_{xx}$), and EPR/NMR spectra showing domain-related broadening and changes across various transition temperatures.
paper_structure: The paper systematically reports on the synthesis methodology to achieve high crystal quality, followed by detailed measurements covering magnetic transitions (domain kinetics via $\chi$), electronic transport ($ho, S$), and local probes of magnetism/localization (EPR, NMR).
why_interesting: Although focused on condensed matter magnetism, the study's deep dive into domain dynamics, localization physics (Anderson insulator), and the interplay between magnetic order and charge carriers provides rich context for understanding correlated electron behavior in novel quantum materials.
